chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The blood money for the erroneous (killing) when the man did not intend it is: one hundred camels, or ten thousand (dirhams) of silver, or one thousand sheep.

And he said: The aggravated blood money (mughallazha) which resembles deliberate killing but is not intentional is higher than the blood money for erroneous killing by the age-categories of camels: thirty-three hiqqah (four-year-old she-camels), thirty-three jadha'ah (five-year-old she-camels), and thirty-four thaniyyah (six-year-old she-camels), all fit for mating with the stallion.

He said: And I asked him about the blood money, and he said: The blood money of a Muslim is ten thousand (dirhams) of silver, or one thousand mithqals of gold, or one thousand sheep according to their ages in three (equal) parts, and one hundred camels according to their ages, and two hundred cows.

key_terms.الثَّنِيَّة: Thaniyyah — a six-year-old she-camel; third age-category in the aggravated diyya specification
key_terms.الْجَذَعَة: Jadha'ah — a five-year-old she-camel; second age-category in the aggravated diyya specification
key_terms.الْحِقَّة: Hiqqah — a four-year-old she-camel; one of the age-categories used in camel diyya payment
key_terms.الْخَطَأ: Khata' — erroneous/unintentional; killing without intent, the lowest category of homicide in Islamic law
key_terms.الْعَمْد: Amd — intentional; deliberate killing that normally requires qisas (retaliation) rather than diyya
key_terms.الْمُغَلَّظَة: Mughallazha — aggravated or enhanced; a category of diyya heavier than khata' but lighter than 'amd (intentional killing), applied to quasi-intentional homicide
key_terms.الْمِثْقَال: Mithqal — a unit of weight (approx. 4.25g); used here for measuring gold in diyya
key_terms.الْوَرِق: Wariq — silver (dirhams); monetary alternative for diyya payment
key_terms.دِيَة: Diyya — blood money or wergild; the financial compensation paid to the family of a victim of homicide or bodily harm

ai.seo_question: What is the amount of diyya (blood money) for intentional and unintentional killing in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies the amounts and forms of diyya (blood money/wergild) for different categories of homicide under Islamic law. Three types are outlined: diyya for unintentional killing (100 camels, 10,000 silver dirhams, or 1,000 sheep); the aggravated diyya for quasi-intentional killing (which resembles intentional but lacks intent), which is higher and specified by the age-categories of camels; and the general diyya of a Muslim broken down across livestock and precious metals. This hadith is part of the classical Shia jurisprudential framework for compensating victims' families and preventing cycles of vengeance.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Wergild of the erroneous (killing) when the man did not intend, is one hundred from the camels, or ten thousand (Dirhams) from the (owners of) the foliage, or a thousand from the sheep’.

And heasws said: ‘The harsh wergild of that which resembles the deliberation, and it is not with deliberation, is higher than the wergild of the erroneous (killing) by the years (ages) of the camel – thirty three Hiqqa (four years old), and thirty Jaz’a (five years old), and thirty four Saniyya (six years old), all of these being easily manageable stallions’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws about the wergild, so heasws said: ‘Wergild of the Muslim is ten thousand from the silver, or a thousand Misqaal (unit or measurement) of gold, or a thousand from the sheep based upon their years being three years, and from the camels based upon their years, and from the cows two hundred’.
